'''Susan E. D'Agostino''' is an American mathematician and science writer, an associate editor at the ''[[Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists]]'', and the author of the book ''How to Free Your Inner Mathematician: Notes on Mathematics and Life'' (2020).{{r|henrich|50y}}

==Education and career==
D'Agostino grew up in [[New York City]].{{r|euler}} After dropping [[calculus]] in high school,{{r|henrich}} she majored in [[anthropology]] at [[Bard College]],{{r|casw}} while working on a dairy farm. At age 25, she set herself a task of earning a mathematics doctorate, beginning with the remedial mathematics missing from her high school education.{{r|henrich}} With the encouragement of mathematician James Henle, she earned a master's degree in [[mathematics education]] at [[Smith College]],{{r|casw|freeing}} and then completed her doctorate at [[Dartmouth College]] in 2003, with a dissertation in [[coding theory]] supervised by Thomas R. Shemanske.{{r|mg}} While a student, she interviewed coding theory pioneer [[Vera Pless]], and won first place in an essay-writing contest of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].{{r|50y}}

Although not originally intending to go on in academia,{{r|henrich}} she took a position as a faculty member at [[Southern New Hampshire University]],{{r|casw}} the first person hired there with a mathematics Ph.D. She worked there for nearly ten years, earning tenure and receiving the university's excellence in teaching award. After the university, formerly a regional teaching school, reinvented itself as an online education provider with a massively increased enrollment, she decided to leave academia, becoming a science writer instead.{{r|henrich}}

In 2018, she was named as a recipient of a Taylor/Blakeslee University Fellowship for graduate study in science writing, from the Council for the Advancement of Science Writing,{{r|casw}} and by 2020, she was studying for a master's degree in science writing from [[Johns Hopkins University]].{{r|50y}} She completed it in 2021, and in the same year became an associate editor for the ''Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists''.{{r|bas}} She also has a [[Master of Fine Arts]] in nonfiction writing from Southern New Hampshire University.{{r|casw}}

==Writing==
D'Agostino has written for "''[[The Atlantic]]'', ''[[The Washington Post]]'', ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]'', ''[[Scientific American]]'', ''[[Quanta Magazine|Quanta]]'', BBC ''Science Focus'', ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', ''[[Financial Times]]'', ''[[Undark Magazine|Undark]]'', ''[[Atlas Obscura]]'', ''[[Discover (magazine)|Discover]]'', ''[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]'', ''[[Literary Hub]]'', and the ''[[Chronicle of Higher Education]]'', among others".{{r|henrich}}

She is the author of the book ''How to Free Your Inner Mathematician: Notes on Mathematics and Life'' (2020).{{r|hfim}} The book received the 2023 [[Euler Book Prize]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].{{r|euler}} She was also editor-in-chief of a book about the [[EDGE program]] for women in mathematics, ''A Celebration of the EDGE Program's Impact on the Mathematics Community and Beyond'' (2019).{{r|henrich|cepi}}
